slides.title: First, reproduce learning in a simpler setting.
slides.notes: Math gives us checkable answers before tackling recursive choices. We use the authors' training code. Their released weights score 366/500 here, versus 371/500 reported. Those are their weights, not our learning gain. The five-answer gap is unexplained.

slides.title: Reward correct attempts, then change the model.
slides.notes: This example is invented. The model generates its own attempts. The checker supplies only final-answer scores. Relative scores guide weight updates. We use eight attempts per question. If all eight scores agree, there is no within-question learning signal.

slides.title: We train on math, then test on different questions.
slides.notes: Short runs use 512 questions and 32 updates. The ongoing run uses 4080 level3-5 questions and plans 255 updates. It also changes the training checker, so this is not duration alone. No added SFT. Monitoring reuses 64 of the 500 test questions.

slides.title: The input format changes the size of the gain.
slides.notes: Each line compares the same two models: original and short chat-trained. Only the test prompt changes between lines. Gains:154 versus12 of500. Separate question-only training adds9 and1. The larger gain is partly prompt-related, not proof all gains are prompt repair.

slides.title: Longer training: an early gain, then little change.
slides.notes: All points:20,42,42,43,43 of64; regraded. Last check:one gain,one loss. Finish255 updates and planned500/AMC/Minerva tests. Next:512-question fresh-base screens, fixed128 test, LR1e-6 versus5e-6, then two learning passes. Small screens guide research, not final claims.
